items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Terminology 105:1
items.html: (To the question) What are the backs of the BAN of BAN? Here, after the Nesira, ZA is discerned as being entirely MAH, namely MAH of MAH and MAH of BAN, meaning the Hochma and Hesed of Aba and the Hochma of the Hesed of Ima. And from the aspect of the names, they are the four aspects in the letters of the Havayah of MAH, which are Keter, Hochma, Bina, and ZA, as above in Answer 2. And the Nukva is entirely BAN, namely the Bina and Gevura of Aba, and the Bina and Gevura of Ima, called the BAN of MAH and the BAN of BAN. And they are only the number and the Gematria of the four aspects in the Havayah of MAH, as above in Answer 2.
